title: Federated Learning Framework Based on Distributed Storage and Diffusion Model for Intrusion Detection on IoT Networks
researchArea: Federated Learning for IoT Intrusion Detection / Decentralized Storage & Data Augmentation
problem: IoT intrusion detection frameworks face severe privacy risks from transmitting raw data [2], single-point-of-failure vulnerabilities in central coordinators [3], and degraded detection performance on minority attack classes caused by heavily imbalanced Non-IID traffic datasets [2, 4].
motivation: Centralized raw traffic aggregation incurs bandwidth costs and violates privacy regulations like GDPR and CCPA [2, 5]. Standard federated learning lacks cost-effective, decentralized model storage [4, 6], while conventional data augmentation techniques (SMOTE, CT-GAN) either create privacy risks or produce synthetic samples that classifiers easily distinguish from real traffic [7-9].
noveltyAndContributions: Integrated a private off-chain Ethereum SWARM decentralized peer-to-peer storage system to fragment, encrypt (Keccak-256/XOR), and distribute model parameters without incurring Ethereum gas fees [2, 4, 10, 11].

Incorporated local tabular diffusion models (Tab-DDPM) at each worker node to generate realistic synthetic tabular samples for minority classes (Theft, Normal), stabilizing non-IID FL training [2, 12-14].

Performed domain-knowledge-driven preprocessing on the BoT-IoT dataset (excluding non-attack ARP traffic and adjusting layer-3 ICMP attributes) and applied Random Forest feature selection to reduce attributes from 43 down to 13 [8, 15-17].
methodology: Constructed a 6-node private P2P FL network (1 concatenator node + 5 worker nodes) connected via socket communication over a Local Area Network [18, 19].
The concatenator node initializes a PyTorch neural network using Xavier uniform initialization, uploads weights to SWARM storage, and broadcasts the UploadFileHash [20].

Worker nodes download model weights, perform local Tab-DDPM diffusion data generation if minority class sample ratios drop below a 10% threshold, train locally, and re-upload updated model chunks to SWARM [14, 20, 21].
The concatenator collects all worker UploadFileHashes from SWARM, aggregates model weights using FedAvg, and redistributes the global updated hash key [18, 20, 22].
keyAssumptions: Worker nodes operate within a secured Local Area Network (LAN) and participate honestly in private SWARM storage without requiring proof-of-work/stake consensus overhead [10, 18].
Tabular diffusion models (Tab-DDPM) can effectively learn complex non-linear network feature distributions without generating distinguishable synthetic artifacts [9, 13, 23].
datasets: MNIST Dataset (used for FL architecture benchmark validation) [2, 19]
partition: IID split (equal class distribution across 5 worker nodes) [17, 25]
Non-IID split (excluding 1 attack class per worker node for BoT-IoT; 2 classes excluded per node for MNIST) [25, 26]
experimentalSetup: 6 virtual machines hosted on an Intel Xeon Silver 4114 server @ 2.20GHz (1 CPU + 2GB RAM per worker VM; 2 CPUs + 2GB RAM for concatenator VM) [19, 27]
80/20 train/test data split evaluated over 150/500 training epochs [28-30]
Custom PyTorch FL pipeline with Tab-DDPM tabular diffusion and private SWARM storage integration [13, 19, 20]
baselines: Flower FL framework (F1 macro 0.98 IID / 0.97 Non-IID on MNIST) [31, 32]
Parallel Processing FL (F1 macro 0.97 on MNIST) [31, 33]
Centralized & FL IDS benchmarks: Popoola et al. (2022) [12], Dharaneish et al. (2024) [34], Thu Huong et al. (2021) [35], Chu & Lin (2023) [36], Hassam Wasswa et al. (2023) [37]
xaiEvaluation: None (The paper focuses on data privacy, decentralized SWARM storage, and diffusion-based tabular data balancing rather than explicit XAI interpretability techniques like SHAP or LIME).
metrics: F1-Score (Primary metric to account for severe class imbalance) [38, 39]
results: Achieved an average macro F1-score of 98.3% on the Non-IID short BoT-IoT dataset (99.0% on IID), significantly boosting minority class F1-scores for Theft (99.6%) and Normal traffic (98.8%) [2, 41, 42]. Outperformed baseline Non-IID FL (Popoola et al., 96.9%) by +1.4% overall and +7.4% on Normal events [42].
failureConditions: High virtual machine resource constraints (1 CPU, 2GB RAM) cause elevated execution time per iteration (29.85s vs 0.94s in single-machine processes) and high diffusion sample generation latency (~32s per sample) [27, 43].
Model aggregation latency at the concatenator node increases when scaling to a large number of participating worker nodes [44].
costEvaluation: Utilized off-chain data storage via Ethereum SWARM instead of on-chain smart contracts, eliminating Ethereum gas transaction fees while keeping model parameters private [4, 10, 45].

limitations.text: Each model upload generates a new hash key; if a node's private key is compromised, unauthorized actors could potentially retrieve model weights and infer sensitive data [46].
Tab-DDPM diffusion data augmentation is computationally intensive (~32 seconds per generated sample on low-spec VMs), presenting deployment challenges for resource-constrained edge devices [43, 47].
Evaluated on 5 worker nodes in a simulated LAN setting and has not yet been validated across multi-segment WAN deployments or real-world IoT datasets like CIC IoT 2023 [44, 48, 49].

futureWork: Implement blockchain-based key management and Ethereum password authentication to secure node access [46, 50].
Develop a hierarchical federated network architecture tailored for large-scale IoT environments [49].
Benchmark the framework on additional IoT datasets such as CIC IoT 2023, CICIDS, and ToN-IoT [48].
Compare diffusion models against lightweight augmentation algorithms (SMOTE, ADASYN) on resource-constrained devices [47].
relevance: Highly relevant to the Federated Learning and Heterogeneous IoT Network Segments pillars of your thesis, offering a practical architecture for handling Non-IID data distributions and decentralized model storage. Note that ARP traffic was explicitly excluded because the BoT-IoT dataset lacks Layer-2 attack scenarios [8, 24].
newIdeas: Combine this paper's Tab-DDPM + SWARM P2P FL architecture with Layer-2 intrusion datasets (such as CL2-IDS from p011) and SHAP feature explainability to build an Explainable Layer-2 Federated IDS.
